title: Lost a python? Boston Animal Care and Control might have it.
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: A ball python, nicknamed 'Tippy,' was found in a Dorchester community food garden near Ellington Street.
Residents reported seeing the snake left in a cage near garden beds, prompting a response from Animal Care and Control.
The python is currently in good condition at the Roslindale animal care facility; information can be reported at 617-635-1800.

title: Tommy DeVito bests Drake Maye, and other takeaways from Patriots’ training camp scrimmage
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Team Blue, led by Tommy DeVito, defeated Team White 22-15 during the Patriots' intra-squad scrimmage at Gillette Stadium.
Tommy DeVito outperformed Drake Maye, completing 13-of-16 passes for two touchdowns, while Maye finished 10-of-19 with two touchdowns.
DeMario Douglas was a standout for Team Blue with six catches, including a deep 50-yard touchdown play from DeVito.

title: A closer look at Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, with nearly 11 miles of shoreline, was voted best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers.
The town has seven villages, over 20 beaches, and activities for all ages and interests.
Highlights include the Port Restaurant's daily oyster specials and scenic views from Saquatucket Marina.

title: DA’s office says prosecutor’s ‘hot mic’ moment in Lindsay Clancy trial was misheard
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Plymouth DA's office clarifies 'hot mic' comment was 'shut it off' regarding autopsy photos, not 'shut her up'.
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington accused prosecutors of inappropriate comments during Lindsay Clancy's emotional courtroom moment.
Judge William Sullivan warned against inappropriate courtroom remarks, emphasizing strict adherence to conduct rules.

title: Little boy dancing to DJ on Boston Common has hundreds of thousands of new fans
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Four-year-old Chukwuemeka Ikesinachi-Nwogwugwu gained viral fame after dancing at a DJ event on Boston Common.
Chukwuemeka's mother posted the video online, receiving over 200,000 likes and 4,000 comments.
The DJ, Miss S. Peace, hosted the Boston Common event to promote human connection, encouraging public participation.

title: Boston wine bar will keep its signature pours, just without the wine
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Barcelona Wine Bar in Boston will use juice and soda for its traditional Spanish porrón pours due to a liquor license suspension.
The bar's license was suspended after serving alcohol to seven underage patrons and observing unsafe serving practices.
Barcelona Wine Bar updated its ID checking policy, ordering more scanners after the police noted improper ID verification.

title: Could Mike Vrabel keep 7 wide receivers on Patriots’ roster?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots may enter the season with seven wide receivers including A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs.
Kayshon Boutte, rumored in trades, remains a potential key player due to strong camp performance.
Kyle Williams expected to play a significant role despite limited camp impact, according to Mike Vrabel.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Suffolk DA candidates Kevin Hayden, Rachael Rollins, and Linda Champion debated over ethics and leadership in Roxbury.
Hayden and Rollins confronted past controversies: Hayden's conflict of interest penalty and Rollins' ethics investigation resignation.
Candidates differ on police accountability; Rollins and Champion seek transparency, while Hayden warns against premature body-camera releases.

title: What Boston meteorologists are saying about this weekend’s humidity levels, the potential for pop-up storms
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: Heat Advisory in effect for southern New England with temperatures near 90°F, feeling like 100°F Friday.
Pop-up showers and storms are possible Friday evening and Saturday evening, with dry conditions expected Sunday.
Humidity levels remain high this weekend, easing gradually late Sunday into Monday with dew points in the 60s.

title: Here’s some background behind the vintage baseball glove a Red Sox fan gave to Aroldis Chapman
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Aroldis Chapman received a vintage Bob Feller model glove from the 1930s as a gift from fan Andy Zides.
The Red Sox rallied five times to win 12-11 against the White Sox in a 13-inning game at Fenway Park.
Chapman allowed a two-run home run, his first earned runs in over a month, before the Red Sox secured victory.
